page: Vultr vx1-m-64c-512gb is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware tradeoff is the local storage configuration, which is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, requiring external storage solutions for data-intensive storage workloads. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong computational capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance reaches 3710.38, placing it in the top 10% of tested servers, while multi-core performance registers at 118152.34, placing it in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read speeds of 532.73 GB/sec and write speeds of 251.91 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. The server also excels in text and data processing, achieving a Passmark database operations score of 42060.8 (top 10%) and a Redis SET throughput of 111.5 million operations per second (top 25%). For language model tasks, the instance processes 135M model prompts at 5494.4 tokens per second and 7B model prompts at 196.77 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-m-64c-512gb offers high memory density and dedicated compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require extensive local disk space. Given the minimal 1 GB local NVMe storage, this server is appropriate for in-memory databases, caching layers, large-scale software compilation, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines where data is fetched from external network storage.
